introduction: At this foundational level, we cover the basic properties of fluids like viscosity and surface tension, and Pascal's law governing fluid pressure at rest. These are highly scoring areas in preliminary exams.

core_concepts.title: Viscosity and Newton's Law
core_concepts.description:
Viscosity is the property of a fluid that offers resistance to its flow (internal friction). 
Newton's Law of Viscosity states that shear stress (tau) is directly proportional to the velocity gradient (du/dy). 
Formula: tau = mu * (du/dy) [Where mu is Dynamic Viscosity].

core_concepts.title: Surface Tension
core_concepts.description:
The property of a liquid surface that causes it to behave like a stretched elastic membrane, attempting to minimize its surface area. 
- Pressure inside a Water Drop: P = 4*sigma / d 
- Pressure inside a Soap Bubble: P = 8*sigma / d 
(Where sigma is surface tension and d is diameter).

core_concepts.title: Pascal's Law and Hydrostatic Pressure
core_concepts.description:
The pressure applied to an enclosed fluid at rest is transmitted equally in all directions. 
Hydrostatic Law: Pressure increases linearly with depth (h). 
Formula: P = rho * g * h (Where rho is density and g is gravity). Hydraulic presses and lifts work strictly on Pascal's Law.

important_entities.name: Manometers
important_entities.significance: Manometers measure pressure by balancing a column of fluid. U-Tube manometers typically use Mercury because of its extremely high density (13.6 g/cm3) and very low vapor pressure, allowing for compact measurements of high pressures.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation:
Exam Trap: Examiners heavily test CGS units of viscosity to confuse students. 
- Dynamic Viscosity (mu): The CGS unit is the Poise (1 Poise = 0.1 Pa-s or N-s/m2). 
- Kinematic Viscosity (nu = mu/rho): The CGS unit is the Stoke (1 Stoke = 10^-4 m2/s).

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: Drop is solid (4), Bubble is hollow (8)
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: A water drop only has one surface (the outside), so the multiplier is 4. A soap bubble is hollow and has two surfaces (inside and outside), so the multiplier doubles to 8.

exam_strategy_tips: A patent SSC JE theoretical question: 'What is the viscosity of an Ideal Fluid?' Answer: Zero.
